newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa says earnings growth higher than 1996.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa says earnings growth higher than 1996.

text.p: A spokesman for German airline Lufthansa AG denied late on Wednesday an unpublished report in German business magazine Capital which he said gave an overly negative impression of the company's finances.
Spokesman Rolf-Dieter Grass told German N-TV all-news television station the company's operating profits in 1996 were nearly 700 million marks and therefore lower than the previous year.
But Grass said they were confident of achieving better results in 1997 and that the first two months of this year already looked promising.
Grass said the magazine report due for publication on Friday was based on some of the company's internal documents which it had obtained.
"This (report) could give the (false) impression that Lufthansa's efforts to restructure the company could fail," Grass said in an interview.
Earlier Lufthansa said in a regulatory statement that its earnings growth would be higher in the current year than in 1996 issued in response to Capital's report.
It said profit in 1996 was estimated at about 700 million marks and in 1995 it earned 756 million marks in ordinary operations.
Business developments were affected by the difficult economic conditions and stiff competition, it said.
Lufthansa is due to announce its annual results for 1996 on May 7.
